title: What is known about 1RB0LE_1RC1RF_1RD0RA_1LE0RC_1LC0LD_0RD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_1RC1RF_1RD0RA_1LE0RC_1LC0LD_0RD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Sampled with the head in C at the left end, the tape is a^n S b^k (a = 1101010, b = 10) and each sweep takes n → n+1, k → k−1; when k runs out a long reorganization rebuilds S and k (observed between steps 7.5·104 and 8.2·106, and between 1.97·107 and 6.48·108). The machine halts only from C> 1 0 1 1 (Lean); in 109 steps A always read a 0 followed by 1 0, never by 1 1.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 62,662 cells have been visited and 30,808 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.04). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.553).

claims.title: The sweeps' shift rules
claims.text: Over the (10)n part C and D shift the words by one cell (01 ↔ 10) going right and D, E run over them going left; over the counter blocks a = 1101010 the head rewrites each block through the phases 0011001, 0101101, 0010011 as it crosses them.

claims.title: The shape of a halt
claims.text: From C> 1 0 1 1 the machine reaches F on a 1 in 3 steps and halts on the next. By reading the table (not formalized): F is entered only from B on a 1, B with a 1 ahead only from A on a 0, and A only from C on a 1, so every halt comes this way.

claims.title: Near misses
claims.text: In 109 steps A reads a 0 5,815,845 times: 5,815,812 times followed by 1 0 1, 16 times by 1 0 0, 17 times at the blank end; never followed by 1 1 (which would halt).

claims.title: The counter and its reorganizations
claims.text: At the samples (C at the left end) the tape reads a^n b^2 a b^10 (a b^2 a b^10)^m ... a b^x a b^y ... a b^k: a pile of n blocks a = 1101010, then a list of numbers written as runs of 10 separated by single a's (pairs like 2, 10 / 16, 32 / 160, 320 / 538, 914 repeat many times), ending with a run bk. Every sweep moves one 10 from the end into a new block a: n+1, k−1, width +5. When k is used up the head stops visiting the left end, works on the right part as an expanding bouncer and rebuilds it with larger numbers; plain counting resumed at steps 8.2·106 (width 5,254) and 6.48·108 (width 49,385).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Halting needs A to read a 0 followed by 1 1, which needs a 0 1 1 where the sweeps keep 0 1 0. Whether some reorganization ever produces it depends on the exact nested numbers, for which no closed rule has been found.

claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LC_1RC0RA_1LA0LD_1LE0RB_1LC1LF_0LA--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0RD_1LC0RA_1LA0LB_1RE0LC_1RA1RF_0RB--- up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 62,662 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
Each sweep moves one cell pair from the right end into the left pile.

sections.eyebrow: What the tape is made of
sections.heading: A pile, a list of numbers, a fuse
html: Write a for the 7-cell word 1101010 and b for 10. Whenever the head is in state C at the left end, the tape has the form
a^n  b^2 a b^10 (a b^2 a b^10)^m  a b^2 a b^34 a b^16 a b^32 a b^109 a b^320 a b^160 ... a b^538 a b^914 ... a b^k

(this one at step 997,019,852, with n = 3291). On the left a pile of n blocks a; in the middle a list of numbers, each written as a run of b's between single a's, with a few pairs repeated many times (2 and 10, 16 and 32, 160 and 320, 538 and 914); at the right end a long run bk, the fuse.

sections.heading: Burning the fuse
html: Between two samples the head sweeps to the right end and back. On the way it shifts every 10 by one cell and rewrites the blocks a through three phases (rules proved in Lean); the net effect is one more block on the pile and one 10 less in the fuse: n → n+1, k → k−1, and the tape grows by 5 cells. Each sweep costs time proportional to the width, which is why the tape grows like the square root of the time.

When the fuse is used up, the head stops coming back to the left end. It works on the right part like an expanding bouncer and rebuilds the list of numbers with a new, much longer fuse. In the run so far this happened between steps 75,408 and 8,170,570, and between 19,673,806 and 648,237,047; each reorganization takes far longer than the counting before it, the signature of a nested counter.

sections.heading: A 0 1 1 that never comes
html: The halting transition is F reading a 1. Following the table backwards, the only way there is C reading 1 0 1 1: C turns its 1 into a 0, A then reads a 0 and B and F read the two 1s. Lean checks that C> 1 0 1 1 halts four steps later. In the first 109 steps A read a 0 almost six million times, always followed by 1 0 (the b-runs keep ones single), never by 1 1. A halt would need a reorganization to leave two ones side by side where A arrives, and no rule for the reorganizations is known yet.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.04). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.553).
After 109 steps the tape spans 62,662 cells (2,162 left of the start, 44,541 right), with a density of 1s of 0.492.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0LC_1RC0RA_1LA0LD_1LE0RB_1LC1LF_0LA---: rename A→D, B→E, C→C, D→A, E→B, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state D, in a mirror
  • 1RB0RD_1LC0RA_1LA0LB_1RE0LC_1RA1RF_0RB---: rename A→D, B→E, C→A, D→B, E→C, F→F; it is this table started in state C
  • 1RB0RC_1LC0LD_1RA0LB_1LE0RA_1LB1LF_0LC---: rename A→D, B→E, C→B, D→C, E→A, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state E, in a mirror

summary: A nested counter: a bouncer moves one 10 per sweep from the right end into a growing pile of blocks 1101010 on the left; when the right end is used up, a long reorganization (an expanding bouncer) rebuilds the right part from a list of numbers.
